Package com.stzteam.features.robotlocalization.fusion

Class LimelightPoseSource

java.lang.Object
com.stzteam.features.robotlocalization.fusion.PoseSource
com.stzteam.features.robotlocalization.fusion.LimelightPoseSource
public class LimelightPoseSource extends PoseSource
A Limelight camera as a pose source.

It reads NetworkTables directly, without LimelightHelpers. That class is a file each team copies into its own repo, not a Maven artifact, so a library cannot depend on it --- and does not need to: we know the whole schema because this feature's own simulator writes it.

As a useful consequence, this source works identically against a physical Limelight and against SimulatedLimelight, with no simulation-specific branch anywhere.

MegaTag1 and MegaTag2

MegaTag1 solves the pose from what it sees alone. MegaTag2 pins the heading with the robot's gyro and solves the rest, which makes it far more stable while turning, but it requires that somebody write the heading to it every cycle. This source does that on its own if you give it a LocalizationInputs.gyroHeading(); it is the most frequently forgotten step and the one that makes MegaTag2 return zeros without explaining why.

With MegaTag2 the heading that comes out is the one you fed in, so it carries no new information: it is worth giving it an enormous heading sigma so the estimator ignores it. That is what megaTag2(String) does by default.

    • megaTag2

      public static LimelightPoseSource megaTag2(String name)
      Creates a MegaTag2 source with the recommended configuration.

      No angular velocity filter --- MegaTag2 copes with turning, which is exactly its reason for existing --- and with the heading sigma saturated so the estimator does not believe a heading it supplied itself.

      Parameters:
      name - the Limelight's table name.
      Returns:
      the source.

    • telemetryDetail

      protected String telemetryDetail()
      Description copied from class: PoseSource
      A free-form detail the subclass can publish alongside the status.

      It exists so RejectionReason.NO_MEASUREMENT is not a dead end: "the source reported nothing" could mean the camera sees no tags, the headset is disconnected, or the timestamp is unusable, and from the dashboard all three look the same.

      Overrides:
      telemetryDetail in class PoseSource
      Returns:
      a short line, or the empty string if there is nothing to add.

    • getAmbiguity

      public OptionalDouble getAmbiguity()
      Description copied from class: PoseSource
      Ambiguity of the last PnP solution, if the source reports it.

      Returning empty --- which is the default behaviour --- means "this source has no such concept", and the ambiguity filter is skipped. That is the right thing for a VIO.
